newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends rollercoaster session mixed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends rollercoaster session mixed.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended mixed in volatile trade Monday as a late-session round of speculative profit taking knocked prices off highs, traders said.

March delivery ended down 0.30 cent at 136.60 cents a lb after ranging between 139.40 and 133.50 cents. Second-position May rose 0.45 cent to 131.75 cents, while the outer months closed 0.70 higher to 2.70 lower.
Profit taking by speculators pressured prices at the opening, in a continued technical correction to recent sharp gains, traders said.
But supply concerns -- and bullish sentiment -- resurfaced Monday afternoon amid news heavy rains could affect Colombia's main coffee harvest in October.

Colombian agronomists said Monday heavy downpours over the last three weeks in the country's principal coffee are delaying the flowering period, which should start in January, and in some cases have partially ruined some plantations.
Traders said news that about 120 truck drivers continued to hold coffee exports "hostage" at Colombia's main Pacific coast port Monday, also fueled buying.
The truckers are demanding "standby" payments for time lost during the nine-day dockworkers' strike that paralyzed the port of Buenaventura until last Friday.
Jose Rios, regional head of the overland cargo transporters association, said about 2,000 tonnes of cargo, 90 percent of it coffee, was affected by the truckers' job action.
After the close, CSCE reported U.S. certified coffee stocks fell by 250 60-kg bags as of Jan. 24, to 21,852 bags.
On the charts, traders pegged March near-term support at 132.00, then 130.00-130.10. Resistance was seen at the contract high of 142.60. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodities Desk 212-859-1640))
